tagline.text: A Bohol coral-stone church rebuilt after the quake in 2021

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,200 (round-trip transport from Tagbilaran plus meals, per person)

children.text: Maribojoc Church is the Santa Cruz parish church in a coastal town of northwest Bohol. It was declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2010, collapsed in the 2013 earthquake, and reopened after restoration in December 2021. It is about 30 minutes by road from Tagbilaran and pairs well with the Punta Cruz Watchtower on Bohol's west coast.

Maribojoc Church is a Roman Catholic church in the town of Maribojoc on the northwest coast of Bohol Island, officially the Santa Cruz (Holy Cross) Parish Church. Its patron is San Vicente Ferrer, and the diocese is said to have designated it a diocesan shrine of San Vicente Ferrer in 2005. Like other old Bohol churches it was a Baroque building of stacked coral stone, described as cruciform with a low four-sided pyramidal roof and an octagonal cupola.

The National Museum declared the church a National Cultural Treasure on May 5, 2010, and in 2009 the National Historical Institute, now the NHCP, installed a historical marker. Then on October 15, 2013, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck Bohol and the building largely collapsed. Only the Sacred Heart image is said to have remained standing, while the image of San Vicente Ferrer was reportedly found unharmed.

Restoration took a long time. The National Museum supervised the reconstruction, rebuilding the church as a faithful copy of the original, and it was reported to have reopened on December 12, 2021. A turnover to the diocese and a Mass led by the papal nuncio were held that day. The ceiling paintings by Raymundo Francia were restored by local artists guided by expert conservators, and the Neo-Gothic and Mudejar-style retablo was recreated with local motifs.
Maribojoc lies about
14km
from central Tagbilaran, along the northern coastal road. Guides give different travel times,
30 minutes to 1 hour

, so allow for traffic. It combines well with tourist stops such as Baclayon Church and the Chocolate Hills, and the Punta Cruz Watchtower in the same town often makes it a half-day trip. Construction dates and restoration details differ among sources and cannot be fixed to one version, so check on-site signs and the latest notices as well.

Bohol's old churches were built of coral stone from the sea, and Maribojoc Church was one of them. It collapsed in the 2013 earthquake and was rebuilt under the supervision of the National Museum to match its former appearance. Because it is a reconstruction, the old weathered texture is not preserved, which is worth knowing before you go.

The Jesuits set up a mission here in the early 17th century, and the parish is said to have been founded in 1767 or 1768 with Fr. Juan Soriano as its first parish priest. The Augustinian Recollects then administered it until 1898. The first church was built from 1798 with forced labor and finished in 1816, and the present church was begun in 1852 under Fr. Manuel Plaza and reported consecrated in 1872. Another source, however, says the Recollects built it in 1886.

The facade is described as having narrow pilasters and niches for saints, with a bas-relief of San Vicente Ferrer at the center. The bell tower is said to hold seven bells and two clock-faced windows.

The metal ceiling inside is painted with catechetical and liturgical motifs. It is attributed to the Cebu painter Raymundo Francia, and local artists reportedly brought it back during the restoration. Because the surface is metal, it feels different from an ordinary mural, so look up and take your time.

The sanctuary and transepts are described as having Neo-Gothic retablos, and the rebuilt version reportedly reflects Mudejar style and local motifs. They contrast with the plain nave walls and draw the eye to the altar.

blocks.title: The convent with a sea view

children.text: A convent building is attached to the back of the church, and the Bohol Sea is said to be visible from there without obstruction. Check locally whether visitors may go in.
The Punta Cruz Watchtower in the same town is known as a coral-stone tower built in 1796 to watch for pirates. It is described as about
3km
from the church. It was damaged in the 2013 earthquake and reportedly restored, so check whether it is open before you visit.

blocks.title: Old fittings and the convent layout

children.text: The old building had a Spanish-era pipe organ in the choir loft (its last performance is given as 1975) and a dome added in 1889, and the clock is said to have been installed in 1893. The convent behind the church is unusual for having an I-shaped layout rather than the common L shape. For which parts were restored and how after the reconstruction, refer to on-site notices.

items.title: Half day from Tagbilaran
items.subtitle: The church and the watchtower together

children.text: Hire a car or van, or a tricycle, in Tagbilaran and head north along the coastal road. It takes about
30 minutes to 1 hour
, so leave some slack.
Arrive at Maribojoc Church and look at the facade, bell tower and the painted ceiling inside. Be quiet during Mass and refrain from taking photos.
Look at the sea view behind the church and, if you like, have a snack at the town market or a restaurant.
Move on to the Punta Cruz Watchtower. It is about
3km
from the church, and there is information that you may have to walk from the entrance, so check locally.
Have lunch in Tagbilaran or a nearby restaurant and continue to your next stop.
Opening hours and entry rules differ among sources and cannot be stated definitively. The watchtower is listed as free from
to
in one source, while another says about ₱50.

children.text: Leave Tagbilaran and see Maribojoc Church first.
After the watchtower and coastal views, head south to visit churches near Loboc or Baclayon.
Continue to Bohol's signature stops such as a Loboc River lunch cruise.
Most of Bohol's churches were restored at different times, so their opening schedules may differ. A hired car is more efficient than public transport for the distances involved.
There are flights from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG). Check airline announcements for routes and schedules.
You can also fly from Manila to Cebu and cross by ferry to Tagbilaran. Ferry services vary by season.
From the airport to Maribojoc, go via Tagbilaran or take a chartered car directly. Check the fare locally.

Take public transport from Tagbilaran and alight in Maribojoc town. Groups can use the
Bohol vehicle tariff
with its
driven compact-car example and arrange church and tower stops in advance.
Tricycles and habal-habal are described as the main transport within Maribojoc town and on the way to the watchtower.
Some sources say ordinary vehicles can go right up to the watchtower entrance. Conditions differ, so check on arrival.
Bohol is best visited in the
November–May
dry season. The church can be seen inside and out and does not depend much on weather, but in the rainy season roads are slippery and frequent rain can slow your travel.
During the hottest period,
April–May
, it is more comfortable to go early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Sunday mornings have Mass and many worshippers, so for sightseeing go on a weekday or avoid Mass times.
We could not confirm the church's feast day or event schedule, so check the diocese's announcements.

Maribojoc town has small lodgings, but most travelers stay in Tagbilaran or on Panglao Island and visit as a day trip. Tagbilaran has many hotels and guesthouses and is close to the airport.
The town has small eateries and a market where you can eat Filipino home cooking. Specific shops change often, so lunch is usually taken in Tagbilaran or toward Loboc. Bring water and a light snack.

After seeing the town, a simple plan is to return along the coastal road to Tagbilaran and eat seafood at a seaside restaurant. Central Tagbilaran has Filipino home cooking, grilled seafood and cafes in one place, so it is convenient for a meal on the way and has plenty of choices if you go straight back to your lodging. On hot days, bring cold drinks in advance.
A church is a place where worshippers pray. Clothes that cover the shoulders and knees are safer than shorts or sleeveless tops.
Be quiet during Mass and refrain from taking photos. Follow the on-site rules on photography.
The building is a reconstruction and its old texture has changed, but knowing the story of how it came through the earthquake makes the visit richer.
The ceiling paintings are high up and hard to see with the naked eye. Small binoculars or a camera zoom help.
If you also want to visit the Punta Cruz Watchtower, hire a vehicle and decide the order of the church and tower beforehand.
Carry cash. There may be few ATMs in town.
The
municipal church museum listing
describes a convent-side collection of religious objects. Ask the parish about current bookings, hours and admission.
Inside, looking slowly in the order of main altar, ceiling paintings and the altar decoration in the two transepts makes it easy to appreciate how well the restored parts have been done.
After visiting the church, you can add a
Maribojoc Abatan River evening tour
. The operator includes a boat and transfers in Panglao or Tagbilaran. Confirm the pickup and boarding points when booking.
If you stay on Panglao, the round trip to Maribojoc takes a long time, so it is more efficient to combine it with Loboc and Baclayon in a single day.
The reconstructed building and its opening hours can change often. Entry may be limited for services and events, so check the latest announcements.
During Mass, visitor access may be restricted or you may be asked to stay quiet. Plan your timing accordingly.
Construction dates vary by source, given as either 1872 or 1886. Rely on the on-site notice.
Parts of the church may be closed because of construction or events.
Midday is very hot, so bring water, a hat and sunscreen.
Fares often need negotiation, so settle the price before you ride.
Baclayon Church
is known as one of the oldest coral-stone churches in Bohol. It forms a church circuit with Maribojoc.
A watchtower from 1796 in the same town, known as a coral-stone tower built to guard against pirates. It is about
3km
from the church.
The
Loboc River
, famous for its lunch buffet cruise, is a staple of Bohol tours.
Tagbilaran City
, Bohol's central city, is the starting point for Maribojoc and has plenty of lodging and restaurants.
